name: Tiroler Kaiserjägermuseum
kurzbeschreibung: The Tiroler Kaiserjägermuseum on Bergisel in Innsbruck: founded in 1880, one of the world's oldest military museums chronicling the four k.u.k. Kaiserjäger regiments.
beschreibung:
Overview

The history-steeped Tiroler Kaiserjägermuseum is situated on the historic Bergisel plateau at 746 meters above sea level in the south of the provincial capital Innsbruck. Embedded in a manicured park setting in immediate proximity to the modern museum complex Das Tirol Panorama and the Bergisel ski jump, the museum serves as the historical memory of the four famous Austro-Hungarian imperial infantry regiments (k.u.k. Tiroler Kaiserjäger). Founded on October 4, 1880, the institution is one of the world's oldest dedicated regimental and military museums and sheds light on a pivotal chapter of Tyrolean and Old Austrian history.

Regimental History & Collections

The elite light infantry branch of the Kaiserjäger was established in 1815 after the Napoleonic Wars of Liberation by Emperor Franz I of Austria as an imperial elite corps. For over a century, its soldiers were recruited predominantly from the mountain valleys of Tyrol and Vorarlberg; in 1895, Emperor Franz Joseph I expanded the corps into four distinct regiments. The Kaiserjäger were renowned for their legendary alpine expertise and deployment as high-mountain troops, yet suffered devastating losses during World War I (1914–1918) on the fronts in Galicia and along the Tyrolean Dolomites front. The museum preserves an exceptional collection of international standing: across multiple floors of the heritage-listed building, over 2,000 original artifacts are showcased, including authentic historic uniforms, masterly oil paintings by renowned war artists such as Albin Egger-Lienz and Thomas Riss, weapons, edged weapons, field equipment, historical photographs, and personal diaries. A poignant memorial space is the Ehrenhalle (Hall of Honor): here rests the monumental Regimentsehrenbuch (Regimental Book of Honor), where the names of all approximately 20,000 Tyrolean Kaiserjäger fallen in the First World War are immortalized on handmade parchment for posterity. The exhibition is complemented by the giant panoramic painting connected underground in the Tirol Panorama.

Visit & Getting There

The Tiroler Kaiserjägermuseum is part of the Tiroler Landesmuseen and is open year-round from Wednesday to Monday, 09:00 to 17:00 (closed on Tuesdays). Admission fees (2025/2026 season): combo ticket for Das Tirol Panorama and Kaiserjägermuseum is €12.00 for adults, €9.00 for seniors and students, while children and youths under 19 enjoy free admission! Admission is complimentary with the Innsbruck Card. Public transit: From Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof, take tram line 1 or 6 to the Bergisel stop or the sightseeing bus TS (The Sightseer Innsbruck) directly to the museum forecourt. By car: A12/A13 motorway (exit Innsbruck Süd or Mitte); paid parking is available at the Bergisel parking lot.

Tips

The museum is connected seamlessly and barrier-free to Das Tirol Panorama via a modern covered corridor equipped with passenger elevators for wheelchair users and strollers. After visiting the exhibitions, a walk along the Bergisel-Panoramaweg is highly recommended, offering breathtaking vistas of the Europabrücke bridge and the Stubaital valley. The on-site restaurant Restaurant 1809 on the museum forecourt serves first-class regional Tyrolean cuisine.
